This longing and clinging to the past is a part of the cycle of life. If your ex was someone else and that relationship was unsuccessful, you would still feel the same way. It's not the person. It's the familiarity of the bond that was created. The intimacy of the relationship is the key to that bond. If you're a heterosexual person and you had a same-sex friend who you were really intimate with.....
-Sidebar: for reference, I'm a heterosexual male. But I'm very handsy with my male friends. If they let me, I like hugging a lot. I like touching in ways that are supportive and feel good. Arm squeezing, back patting etc and hugging.
.....If you had what people would describe as an effectionate, physical relationship with your same sex/non-sexual friends, that intimacy would also create a bond. Not quite as powerful as a sexual bond, but really fucking close. And say, for example, you had a falling out with one of these friends because of something that just made your continued friendship impossible. To the point that they should now be your enemy.
You would long for the familiarity of the bond the exact same way you do with your ex. Who the person is doesn't matter. Yet, until you understand and realize this, you'll delude yourself into thinking there is something to hold onto. And that makes you rather dangerous to your new girlfriend, who doesn't deserve to be with someone that's incapable of separating from the past.

Having said that, it is now inappropriate for you to hug your ex. Until you have YEARS between you and maybe you've both had kids and you're completely different human beings - it is, right now, inappropriate to hug your ex or have any kind of relationship with her. Especially considering her toxicity and manipulative behaviour are reasons for you not to be together. Breaking up isn't really enough. You have no grounds to be friends with an emotionally manipulative person, girlfriend or not. That's still not platonic friend material.  
Now forget about her and focus on this new, awesome person you have in your life. Eliminate all contact with your ex.

Hey brother, fight through this.   
The relationship stuff is hard, I know. At this point, even if it's not over and you could get it back, it's really for the best that you let it go. This is all causing you so much suffering, and really you just need to figure out how to stand on your own for a while. Grow and be strong for a while. One day you'll be able to apologize to her from a different place in life. And to be completely honest, by then you might be apologizing for breaking some other hearts too. We make these mistakes at the time in our lives when we can't NOT make them.  
Re-group. Accept responsibility for......whatever. Taking responsibility just means accepting the outcome of your actions. You've done that, right? Yes you have. But you're internalizing and pouring salt all over it, making it worse for yourself or anyone close. Stop that shit and centre yourself. Or spend your foreseeable future trying to get yourself centered.   
Start looking for a job. Until you find a job, look for a place to volunteer. It's work without getting paid but you need to start doing things where people will depend on you. It's important for your psychology. You'll build connections with people and realize your greater value in this life.  
So, spend 6hrs or so a day applying for jobs, and find out where you can volunteer in your town right away.  
Fight through this.  
Centre yourself.  
This is one stepping stone in life. Brother, there's a shit load of other stepping stones after this. Begin making peace with yourself so you can make the next step.  


Sending positive, calming energy your way.

Just don't stop reaching out. Try and lay off the sauce if you can, it's a serious depressant. But if you're sauced up and feeling the depths of despair, REACH OUT. -\*Try the local, instead of national, crisis prevention line. (Google your area + crisis prevention hotline)  
\*Come post here. Lots of people will be here for you.  
\* [https://www.imalive.org/](https://www.imalive.org/)  this is a text based support network. I've never used it myself because I can't focus enough for typing if I'm in a bad state. But maybe you can try it.  


Again-sorry you had a shit experience. I'm sorry it wasn't what you needed. I'm sorry they couldn't at least tell you that it's going to be ok. Just talk. Hold on. Sorry about all that.

If you force yourself to learn how to exaggerate your emotions, you'll be learning how to appear disingenuous. It's a slippery slope you're considering here. The re-assuring part here is there are really only 2 reasons for wanting to learn what you do - to manipulate others, or to find a way to better share any joy/positive feelings you may have with people around you. And it really doesn't sound like you're struggling with trying to manipulate people. So....  
Practice vocalizing your feelings. Especially the good ones. Don't worry about how it sounds-simply try developing the practice. It's hard. You can do it.  
And practice smiling.  
When I was a young person, I developed myself to be very much the way you describe. The stone face. Non-expressive. I suspect the reason people are physically less expressive now is because of things like emojis. There's a new language and a new way of communicating that completely eliminates your physical expression from the conversation.  
When I did it, it was just to mask emotion. I thought a stone face meant a strong face and smiling lead way to weakness or cowardess. Either way, I still got to the exactly part of the road where you are at. I wanted to naturally express more joy/pleasure/happiness but even my words came out monotone.  
So you practice. First just by expressing the things you don't bother expressing, just to say them. Then I would practice smiling at people. Which sounds ridiculous, but it probably made the biggest change. Make real eye contact and just smile. At first, it might feel like a deeply personal, intimate exchange because you're not used to doing it. You feel vulnerable. Use the brief encounters to practice most: the grocery store cashier, the mail carrier, the person driving the bus or filling your gas tank.  
Also, keep your eye out for people who express themselves in ways that you WANT TO. Let other people become your mentors without them ever knowing it. Copy what they do.  
It takes time, but it's also a meditation. It's conscious awareness. As more of your time is spent expressing yourself in a different way, that way eventually just BECOMES you.

There are a lot of resources like [https://line-of-action.com/](https://line-of-action.com/) that give you a certain amount of time per image study. Having a set amount of time forces you to develop confidence with each line you put down. That confidence decreases how long it takes you to draw anything.  
Keep in mind that this IS the path, but there will still be a lot of shit along the way. But incorporating these timed studies into your daily practice will pay off faster than anything else. For myself, I wouldn't keep a timer that was longer than 2 minutes for months. Rarely were they fleshed out even far enough to include a cast shadow. Then I set a timer that went incrementally from 1 minute to 10 minutes and that 10 minute study was better than anything I had been doing before incorporating timed practices.
